Chapter 9: Reclaiming Joy and Creating New Traditions.
Healing from toxic parenting isn’t just about steering clear of pain. It’s about something much deeper—reclaiming your right to experience joy, connection, and true fulfillment.
Have you ever noticed, after years of just getting by, how easy it is to lose touch with what actually makes life meaningful? Let’s take a look at how you can rediscover pleasure, build new traditions, and cultivate a real sense of belonging.
First, start by giving yourself permission to seek joy—even in the smallest ways. Maybe that means taking a walk in nature, diving into a hobby you’ve always loved, or simply sharing a laugh with a friend.
Don’t let anyone tell you joy is frivolous. It’s not. In fact, it’s a vital part of healing and building resilience.
Now, let’s talk about traditions. If holidays or family rituals bring up old pain, why not create your own celebrations? Imagine hosting a “friendsgiving,” or starting a gratitude journal just for yourself. Or maybe you mark important milestones with personal rituals that really resonate with your values.
Here are a few gentle ways to nurture joy and connection in your daily life:
Mindful presence. Savor those simple pleasures—a warm cup of tea, a favorite song, that feeling of sunlight on your face.
Acts of kindness. Try volunteering, helping a neighbor out, or offering genuine support to someone who needs it.
Building community. Seek out groups or activities that make you feel seen and valued for who you are.
Of course, it’s completely natural to grieve what was lost—or what you never received—from your family of origin. But remember, you have the power to create new sources of comfort and meaning. Over time, these new experiences can actually help rewrite your emotional landscape, making space for hope and possibility.
Here’s something to keep in mind: joy and pain can exist side by side. Allowing yourself to feel both isn’t a weakness—it’s a sign of real growth.
By embracing the full range of your human experience, you’re reclaiming agency over your own story.
